metadata.title: A Lipschitz-nonincreasing deformation of small unitary-valued maps
metadata.description:
For the unit-round sphere and either the unnormalized Hilbert–Schmidt or operator-norm length metric on U(N), this note gives an explicit strong deformation retraction of the maps with Lipschitz constant at most 1/2 onto the constant maps. At time t in [0,1], the Lipschitz constant is at most (1-t²)/(1+t²) times its original value. The formula is continuous in the entire input map, fixes constant maps, preserves the strict sublevel, and stays in the original U(N). It supplies an affirmative answer to the literal assertion in Gromov’s 2017 question [?24](i), catalogued as AMR-066-0025.

The proof is elementary matrix algebra plus an intrinsic curve-length argument. The Cayley/Möbius transformation is classical. Ordinary contraction without preservation of the Lipschitz sublevel already follows from a standard logarithm chart. A documented, bounded literature search located no earlier explicit resolution or exact quantitative map-space retraction; first-publication priority is not established.

The package includes the four-page preprint, editable LaTeX source, independent AI-assisted internal reviews, a priority audit, dependency-free exact algebra checks, optional NumPy stress tests, and SHA-256 checksums. The scripts are finite diagnostics, not a formal proof of the theorem. This is an unrefereed preprint developed and checked with generative-AI assistance. Paper and prose: CC BY 4.0; code: MIT.
